label: Activate triggers
description: Turn on triggers: the program's own, or with `instance` that instance's per-instance triggers, releasing or dropping what they held while they were down (`held`). A trigger reading an infra copy needs that copy running first; triggers already on are left alone.

inputs.name: instance
inputs.description: Whose triggers: an instance id your program gives it (`user-42`), for that instance's per-instance triggers. Unwired: the program's own triggers, the ones shared by every instance. Wired, and no id arrives (the node feeding it did not run): this node skips.

inputs.name: only
inputs.description: Only these triggers, named as the program writes them. Unwired: all of them (every shared trigger, or every per-instance trigger of the instance).

inputs.name: held
inputs.label: Held work
inputs.description: The work the triggers held while they were down (events that arrived, runs they fired that are paused on a wait): run releases it, paced at half each trigger's own limits so new arrivals still get through; drop deletes the events and cancels the paused runs.

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: True once the triggers are on.

then.message: ActivateTriggers '{id}' names {names} in `only`, which is no per-instance trigger of this program. It is given an `instance`, so it acts on that instance's triggers: name each the way the program writes it (`inbox`, `work.inbox` inside a group, or `one.inbox` inside an included file), or leave `instance` unwired to act on the program's own triggers.

It has no `instance`, so it acts on the program's own triggers: name each the way the program writes it (`inbox`, `work.inbox` inside a group, or `one.inbox` inside an included file), or wire `instance` to act on an instance's per-instance triggers.
